In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mannose-binding lectins are involved in the pathogenesis of ischemic stroke and that the effects of MBL are secondary to intracerebral thrombosis and reduced cerebral blood flow.

mannose-binding lectins are involved in thrombus formation in ischemic brain tissue and may be a potential therapeutic target in the future.

MBL is involved in thrombosis after brain ischemia and that MBL-deficient mice are protected against brain damage.
